properties.displayName: [DefenseEvasion] BYOVD driver file or suspicious msimg32.dll on disk (Qilin / Warlock context)
properties.description:
DO NOT EDIT IN PORTAL - MANAGED VIA GIT REPO.

Detects file activity consistent with bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver (BYOVD) and related ransomware
tradecraft reported for Qilin and Warlock operations: kernel drivers such as hlpdrv.sys, rwdrv.sys,
NSecKrnl.sys, or googleApiUtil64.sys under a drivers path, or msimg32.dll created/renamed outside the
legitimate Windows System32/SysWOW64 locations (possible DLL side-loading staging).

Context: Public reporting describes Qilin using hlpdrv.sys / rwdrv.sys and msimg32.dll side-loading;
Warlock activity has included NSecKrnl.sys and historically googleApiUtil64.sys for kernel-level
security product termination.

Analyst actions:
1. Confirm the file hash against threat intel; review initiating process and parent chain on the device.
2. Check for related service creation (sc.exe), image loads, and EDR telemetry gaps on the same host.
3. If confirmed malicious, escalate to the Security Operations Center (SOC) Manager for investigation.
properties.query:
// The query_now parameter represents the time (in UTC) at which the scheduled analytics rule ran to produce this alert.
let query_now = now();
let lookback = 4h;
let suspiciousDrivers = dynamic([
"hlpdrv.sys",
"rwdrv.sys",
"NSecKrnl.sys",
"googleApiUtil64.sys"
]);
// Exclude common benign Windows servicing / recovery mount paths (covers $WinREAgent\Scratch\Mount\Windows\WinSxS\...)
let benignServicingPathIndicators = dynamic([
@"\$WinREAgent",
@"\Scratch\Mount\Windows",
@"\WinSxS",
@"\Windows\Servicing",
@"\SoftwareDistribution"
]);
// Exclude common benign servicing processes (covers dismhost.exe)
let benignInitiators = dynamic([
"dismhost.exe",
"dism.exe",
"tiworker.exe",
"trustedinstaller.exe",
"wuauclt.exe",
"usoclient.exe",
"poqexec.exe"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated between (query_now - lookback .. query_now)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed")
| extend
  FileNameLower = tolower(FileName),
  FolderPathLower = tolower(FolderPath),
  InitProcLower = tolower(InitiatingProcessFileName),
  InitCmdLine = coalesce(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, "")
| extend
  // True if the file operation occurred in known benign servicing / recovery staging locations
  IsBenignServicingPath = FolderPathLower has tolower(@"$WinREAgent")
      or FolderPathLower has tolower(@"\scratch\mount\windows")
      or FolderPathLower has tolower(@"\winsxs")
      or FolderPathLower has tolower(@"\windows\servicing")
      or FolderPathLower has tolower(@"\softwaredistribution"),
  // True if initiated by known benign Windows servicing processes
  IsBenignInitiator = InitProcLower in~ (benignInitiators)
| extend DetectionReason = case(
  // BYOVD-ish driver names dropped/renamed into drivers path
  FileNameLower in~ (suspiciousDrivers)
      and (FolderPathLower has @"\windows\system32\drivers" or FolderPathLower has @"\drivers"),
  "Known_BYOVD_or_reported_ransomware_driver_name_in_drivers_path",
  // msimg32 outside normal system dirs, excluding known benign servicing/mount ops and servicing initiators
  FileNameLower == "msimg32.dll"
      and not(FolderPathLower has @"\windows\system32" or FolderPathLower has @"\windows\syswow64")
      and not(IsBenignServicingPath)
      and not(IsBenignInitiator),
  "msimg32_dll_outside_system_locations_possible_side_load_staging",
  "Other"
)
| where DetectionReason != "Other"
| extend SHA256Display = iif(isempty(SHA256), "(none)", SHA256)
| project
  TimeGenerated,
  DeviceName,
  DeviceId,
  ActionType,
  FileName,
  FolderPath,
  SHA256 = SHA256Display,
  InitiatingProcessAccountUpn,
  InitiatingProcessFileName,
  InitiatingProcessCommandLine = InitCmdLine,
  DetectionReason

properties.displayName: [DefenseEvasion] msimg32.dll loaded from non-system path (possible side-load)
properties.description:
DO NOT EDIT IN PORTAL - MANAGED VIA GIT REPO.

Fires when msimg32.dll is loaded into a process from a path other than the legitimate Windows
System32 or SysWOW64 locations. Reporting on Qilin ransomware describes abuse of a malicious
msimg32.dll delivered via DLL side-loading as part of a chain that can disable EDR.

This rule focuses on image load telemetry (proof the module was actually loaded), which is
stronger signal than file-create alone.

Analyst actions:
1. Review InitiatingProcessFileName and InitiatingProcessFolderPath — is the loader a signed,
   expected application or something from Temp/Downloads?
2. Pivot on DeviceId for same-window DeviceFileEvents and DeviceProcessEvents.
3. If malicious, isolate the host and hunt for companion BYOVD drivers or service installs.
properties.query:
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(4h)
| where FileName =~ "msimg32.dll"
| where not(
    FolderPath has @"\Windows\System32\msimg32.dll"
    or FolderPath has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\msimg32.dll"
  )
| extend
    LoaderPath = strcat(InitiatingProcessFolderPath, @"", InitiatingProcessFileName),
    InitiatingAccount = strcat(InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, @"", InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    DeviceName,
    DeviceId,
    ImageLoadedPath = FolderPath,
    FileName,
    InitiatingProcessFileName,
    InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
    InitiatingProcessId,
    InitiatingAccount,
    LoaderPath

properties.displayName: [Execution] Warlock / ransomware-associated tooling or kernel service command line
properties.description:
DO NOT EDIT IN PORTAL - MANAGED VIA GIT REPO.

Detects process command lines associated with tooling called out in public reporting on Warlock
ransomware activity (e.g. PsExec-style usage, TightVNC server, rclone, Cloudflare tunnel client,
sc.exe creating/starting a kernel driver service). Also flags command lines referencing known BYOVD
driver file names (hlpdrv.sys, rwdrv.sys) for correlation with file and image-load rules.

This is intentionally pattern-based and may require tuning for approved IT remote support or
backup tools. Document exemptions via suppression or allowlists after review.

Analyst actions:
1. Classify the account (user vs service) and whether execution is expected on this device class.
2. Correlate with DeviceFileEvents / DeviceImageLoadEvents on the same DeviceId and timeframe.
3. For rclone or tunnel clients on servers, treat as high priority for exfiltration / C2 review.
properties.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(4h)
| where ActionType == "ProcessCreated"
| extend pcl = tolower(ProcessCommandLine)
| extend MatchedPattern = case(
    pcl has "psexec" or pcl has "psexesvc", "PsExec_style",
    pcl has "tvnserver" or pcl has "winvnc" or pcl has "tightvnc", "TightVNC_style",
    pcl has "rclone", "Rclone",
    pcl has "cloudflared" or pcl has "cloudflare tunnel" or pcl has "tunnel run", "Cloudflare_tunnel_style",
    pcl has "velociraptor" or pcl has "velociraptor.exe", "Velociraptor_reference",
    pcl has "yuze" and (pcl has "proxy" or pcl has "reverse"), "Yuze_style_keyword",
    (pcl has "sc " and (pcl has "create" or pcl has "start") and pcl has ".sys"), "sc_kernel_driver_service",
    pcl has "hlpdrv.sys" or pcl has "rwdrv.sys", "BYOVD_driver_name_in_command_line",
    "None"
  )
| where MatchedPattern != "None"
| extend
    AccountDisplay = coalesce(AccountName, AccountDomain, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, "(unknown)")
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    DeviceName,
    DeviceId,
    MatchedPattern,
    FileName,
    FolderPath,
    ProcessCommandLine,
    AccountDisplay,
    InitiatingProcessFileName,
    InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
    InitiatingProcessAccountUpn

properties.displayName: [Exfiltration] Files Copied to USB (Blocked by Policy)
properties.description:
Alerts when a user attempts to copy files to removable media (USB) and the action is blocked by policy.
This remains important for visibility into attempted exfiltration and policy bypass attempts.

If you believe there is a data exfiltration risk (e.g., file names referencing customer lists, prospects, or company IP),
escalate to a SOC Engineer or Incident Handler immediately.
properties.query:
// Get ICESD watchlist users to exclude (case-insensitive match on Name column)
let ExcludedICESDUsers = _GetWatchlist('ICESD') | project Name = tolower(tostring(Name));
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCopiedToRemovableMedia"
// Exclude ICESD users
| where tolower(AccountDisplayName) !in (ExcludedICESDUsers)
// 1) Normalize fields from RawEventData (stringify first to avoid type/casting issues)
| extend
    FileName            = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectId),
    USBdetails          = tostring(RawEventData.RemovableMediaDeviceAttributes),
    FileExtension       = tostring(RawEventData.FileExtension),
    DestinationLocation = tostring(RawEventData.TargetFilePath),
    PolicyInfo          = tostring(RawEventData.PolicyMatchInfo),
    EnforcementModeRaw  = tostring(RawEventData.EnforcementMode),
    SensitivityLabelRaw = tostring(RawEventData.SensitivityLabelEventData),
    DeviceDetails       = tostring(RawEventData.DeviceName)
// 2) Interpret enforcement: "4" (or 4) is commonly 'Blocked' in device control/DLP semantics
| extend EnforcementModeNum = iff(EnforcementModeRaw matches regex @"^\d+$", toint(EnforcementModeRaw), toint(extract(@"^(\d+)", 1, EnforcementModeRaw)))
| extend Action = case(EnforcementModeNum == 4, "Blocked", tostring(EnforcementModeRaw))
// 3) Map well-known label GUIDs to readable names (fallback to raw value)
| extend LabelName = case(
      SensitivityLabelRaw == "6b471bfd-f628-4d09-bd36-e4014ade38e5", "Limited Access - Internal Staff Only",
      SensitivityLabelRaw == "2bc8e810-0e48-4510-a73b-a00cf068b73d", "Creditsafe Eyes Only",
      SensitivityLabelRaw == "08181d91-44f1-4c8a-a789-226d3eeb0820", "Limited Access - External and Internal",
      SensitivityLabelRaw == "900e61c5-9326-4775-9dd5-9a546e043cca", "Public (Anyone Can View)",
      tostring(SensitivityLabelRaw)
  )
// 4) Keep only 'Blocked' actions
| where Action == "Blocked"
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    AccountDisplayName,
    DeviceDetails,
    ActionType,
    Action,
    FileName,
    FileExtension,
    DestinationLocation,
    LabelName,
    PolicyInfo,
    USBdetails,
    IPAddress,
    City,
    CountryCode,
    ISP

properties.displayName: [Exfiltration] Testing - Files copied to USB with 'Creditsafe Eyes Only' or 'Limited Access - Internal Staff Only'
properties.description:
Detects cases where files labeled “Creditsafe Eyes Only” or “Limited Access – Internal Staff Only”
were copied to a removable (USB) device. Investigate the files, user, and device; if suspicious,
escalate to a senior SOC member.
properties.query:
// Get ICESD watchlist users to exclude (case-insensitive match on Name column)
let ExcludedICESDUsers = _GetWatchlist('ICESD') | project Name = tolower(tostring(Name));
// Detect high-sensitivity labeled files copied to removable/USB targets
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "FileCopiedToRemovableMedia"
// Exclude ICESD users
| where tolower(AccountDisplayName) !in (ExcludedICESDUsers)
// Extract fields from RawEventData
| extend
    FileName          = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectId),
    SensitivityLabelId = tostring(RawEventData.LabelId),
    USBdetails        = tostring(RawEventData.RemovableMediaDeviceAttributes),
    FileExtension     = tostring(RawEventData.FileExtension)
// Filter to the two specific labels
| where SensitivityLabelId in (
      "2bc8e810-0e48-4510-a73b-a00cf068b73d", // Creditsafe Eyes Only
      "6b471bfd-f628-4d09-bd36-e4014ade38e5"  // Limited Access - Internal Staff Only
  )
// Map label GUIDs to human-readable names
| extend LabelName = case(
      SensitivityLabelId == "6b471bfd-f628-4d09-bd36-e4014ade38e5", "Limited Access - Internal Staff Only",
      SensitivityLabelId == "2bc8e810-0e48-4510-a73b-a00cf068b73d", "Creditsafe Eyes Only",
      tostring(SensitivityLabelId)
  )
// Enhanced summarization with more context
| summarize 
    FilesCopied = count(),
    FirstCopy = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastCopy = max(TimeGenerated),
    UniqueFiles = dcount(FileName),
    FileTypes = make_set(FileExtension, 10),
    SampleFiles = make_list(FileName, 10),
    USBDevices = make_set(USBdetails, 5)
  by AccountDisplayName, LabelName
| where FilesCopied >= 50
| extend 
    RiskLevel = case(
        LabelName == "Creditsafe Eyes Only" and FilesCopied >= 100, "CRITICAL",
        LabelName == "Creditsafe Eyes Only", "HIGH",
        FilesCopied >= 200, "HIGH",
        "MEDIUM"
    ),
    TimeSpan = format_timespan(LastCopy - FirstCopy, "hh:mm:ss")
| project
    TimeGenerated = LastCopy,
    AccountDisplayName,
    LabelName,
    RiskLevel,
    FilesCopied,
    UniqueFiles,
    TimeSpan,
    FirstCopy,
    LastCopy,
    FileTypes,
    SampleFiles,
    USBDevices

This is an alert for when files with risky file names have been copied to an USB. This alert is only alerting for the allowed action and not the file names. Please review file names for risky items such as client, customer or prospect. 

If you believe there to be a data exfiltration risk please raise to SOC Engineer or Incident handler as soon as possible.
properties.query:
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType contains "FileCopiedToRemovableMedia" 
| extend FileName = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectId)
| extend USBdetails = tostring(RawEventData.RemovableMediaDeviceAttributes)
| extend FileExtension = tostring(RawEventData.FileExtension)
| extend DestinationLocation = tostring(RawEventData.TargetFilePath)
| extend PolicyInfo = tostring(RawEventData.PolicyMatchInfo)
| extend EnforcementMode = tostring(RawEventData.EnforcementMode)
| extend SensitivityLabel = tostring(RawEventData.SensitivityLabelEventData)
| extend DeviceDetails = tostring(RawEventData.DeviceName)
| where EnforcementMode contains "1"
| extend LabelName = replace_strings(
SensitivityLabel,
dynamic ( ['6b471bfd-f628-4d09-bd36-e4014ade38e5', '2bc8e810-0e48-4510-a73b-a00cf068b73d', '08181d91-44f1-4c8a-a789-226d3eeb0820', '900e61c5-9326-4775-9dd5-9a546e043cca']),
dynamic (['Limited Access/Limited Access - Internal Staff Only', 'Creditsafe eyes only', 'Limited Access/Limited Access - External And Internal', 'Public (Anyone Can View)']))
| extend Action= replace_strings(
EnforcementMode,
dynamic (["1"]),
dynamic (["Allowed"]))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceDetails,PolicyInfo, FileName,Action,LabelName,FileExtension,DestinationLocation,USBdetails,ISP,City,CountryCode,IPAddress,AccountDisplayName,ActionType

properties.description:

If anything looks like a genuine data exfiltration incident please inform a member of the Purple Team or the Security Operations Manager immediately

                     EnforcementMode,

                     dynamic(["Allowed", "blocked"])

| where not(UploadDomain in ("blackline", "recruiterflow", "pwc", "eu-west-1.console.aws.amazon.com", "csceproduction.crm4.dynamics.com", "prod1.ar-eu.blackline.com", "apps.docusign.com", "central.connect.pwc.com", "dev.azure.com", "acrobat.adobe.com", "chatgpt.com", "capi.grammarly.com", "mtalk.google.com", "www.linkedin.com", "localhost", "m365.cloud.microsoft"))

    Action,
    FileName = ObjectID1,
    FileExtension,
    Application1,

    CountryCode,

properties.displayName: [CredentialAccess] A User Has Read a BitLocker Key in Azure
properties.description:
A user has read a BitLocker key in Azure. This action may expose recovery secrets.
Standard users typically have no reason to read these keys. Service desk users are excluded.

Investigate why this user accessed a BitLocker key. Correlate the Device ID to determine
which device the key belongs to and validate whether the access was legitimate.
properties.query:
// Get ICESD watchlist users to exclude (case-insensitive match on Name column)
let ExcludedICESDUsers = _GetWatchlist('ICESD') | project Name = tolower(tostring(Name));
AuditLogs
| where OperationName == "Read BitLocker key"
| extend ActorUPN = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend Additional = tostring(AdditionalDetails[0].value)
| parse Additional with * "ID: '" KeyId "'" *
| parse Additional with * "device: '" DeviceId "'" *
| extend 
    ActorName = tostring(split(ActorUPN, "@")[0]),
    ActorUPNSuffix = tostring(split(ActorUPN, "@")[1])
| where tolower(ActorName) !in (ExcludedICESDUsers)
// Enrich with device name from DeviceInfo table
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion) by AadDeviceId
    | project AadDeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion
) on $left.DeviceId == $right.AadDeviceId
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    OperationName,
    ActorUPN,
    ActorName,
    ActorUPNSuffix,
    KeyId,
    DeviceId,
    DeviceName = coalesce(DeviceName, "Unknown"),
    OSPlatform,
    OSVersion,
    Additional

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: [CredentialAccess] User read BitLocker key in Azure

properties.displayName: Changes to Application Ownership
properties.description:
Detects changes to the ownership of an appplicaiton.
  Monitor these changes to make sure that they were authorized.
  Ref: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/entra/architecture/security-operations-applications#new-owner
properties.query:
AuditLogs
  | where Category =~ "ApplicationManagement"
  | where OperationName =~ "Add owner to application"
  | extend InitiatingAppName = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName)
  | extend InitiatingAppServicePrincipalId = tostring(InitiatedBy.app.servicePrincipalId)
  | extend InitiatingUserPrincipalName = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
  | extend InitiatingAadUserId = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.id)
  | extend InitiatingIPAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
  | extend TargetUserPrincipalName = TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName
  | extend TargetAadUserId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
  | extend mod_props = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties
  | mv-expand mod_props
  | where mod_props.displayName =~ "Application.DisplayName"
  | extend TargetAppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(mod_props.newValue)))
  | where TargetAppName !contains "Microsoft Copilot Studio"
  | extend AddedUser = TargetUserPrincipalName
  | extend UpdatedBy = iif(isnotempty(InitiatingAppName), InitiatingAppName, InitiatingUserPrincipalName)
  | extend InitiatingAccountName = tostring(split(InitiatingUserPrincipalName, "@")[0]), InitiatingAccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(InitiatingUserPrincipalName, "@")[1])
  | extend TargetAccountName = tostring(split(TargetUserPrincipalName, "@")[0]), TargetAccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(TargetUserPrincipalName, "@")[1])
  | project-reorder TimeGenerated, InitiatingAppName, InitiatingAppServicePrincipalId, InitiatingAadUserId, InitiatingUserPrincipalName, InitiatingIPAddress, TargetAppName, AddedUser, UpdatedBy

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Changes to Application Ownership

Compression can be legitimate, but on high-risk users it may indicate data staging or exfiltration.

| where FileName in~ ("winrar.exe", "7z.exe", "winzip.exe")

    FolderPath,
    ProcessCreationTime,
    ProcessCommandLine,
    ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
    InitiatingProcessFileName,
    InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
    InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
    InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
    InitiatingProcessMD5,
    InitiatingProcessSHA256,
    InitiatingProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName,

properties.displayName: [Exfiltration] Leavers Sending Attachments to Personal Email Domains
properties.description:
This alert triggers when a user listed in the "High_Risk_Watchlist" sends an email containing an attachment
to an external email domain commonly associated with personal or non-corporate use.
properties.query:
let HighRiskSenders = _GetWatchlist('High_Risk_Watchlist') 
    | project SearchKey = tolower(tostring(SearchKey));
let ExternalDomains = dynamic([
    "gmail.com","outlook.com","yahoo.com","icloud.com","hotmail.com","qq.com","protonmail.com",
    "aol.com","zoho.com","mail.com","gmx.com","yandex.com","tutanota.com","mail.ru",
    "live.com","msn.com","naver.com","163.com","ymail.com","fastmail.com","sky.com","bt.com"
]);
let ImageExtensions = dynamic([".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".gif", ".bmp", ".svg", ".tiff"]);
EmailEvents
| where AttachmentCount > 0
| extend SenderLower = tolower(SenderFromAddress)
| where SenderLower in (HighRiskSenders)
| extend RecipientDomain = tolower(extract(@"@(.+)$", 1, RecipientEmailAddress))
| where RecipientDomain in (ExternalDomains)
// Join with filtered Attachment table
| join kind=inner (
    EmailAttachmentInfo
    // Fixed: Using 'not' function for better compatibility
    | where not(FileName has_any (ImageExtensions))
    | project NetworkMessageId, FileName, FileType, FileSize
) on NetworkMessageId
| extend 
    FileSizeMB = round(FileSize / 1048576.0, 2),
    RiskLevel = case(
        FileSize > 50000000, "HIGH",     // >50MB
        FileSize > 10000000, "MEDIUM",   // >10MB
        "LOW"
    )
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    SenderFromAddress,
    RecipientEmailAddress,
    RecipientDomain,
    Subject,
    FileName,
    FileType,
    FileSize,
    FileSizeMB,
    RiskLevel,
    AttachmentCount,
    NetworkMessageId,
    ReportId

properties.description:
This alert triggers when a user sends an email to a personal email domain that contains an
attachment with high‑risk or sensitive keywords in the filename. This may indicate attempted
data exfiltration or a violation of data handling policies.
properties.query:
let SensitiveWords = dynamic([
    "Customer","Kundenliste","Klient","Kund","Klant","Client","Kunde","Cliente",
    "kokayku","Kuraianto","Risuto","Clienti","prospect","prospetti","Interessentenliste",
    "prospekt","enrich","Angereichert","Enriquecido","Arricchito","Berik","Beriget",
    "Rikastettu","portfolio","Portefeuille","Portfölj"
]);
let InternalDomains = dynamic([
    "creditsafe.com","creditsafe.be","creditsafe.co.in","creditsafe.co.jp","creditsafe.fi",
    "creditsafe.dk","creditsafe.fr","creditsafe.hu","creditsafe.ie","creditsafe.it",
    "creditsafe.lu","creditsafe.mail.onmicrosoft.com","creditsafe.nl","creditsafe.no",
    "creditsafe.se","creditsafede.com","creditsafenl.com","creditsafeuk.com","creditsafeusa.com"
]);
let PersonalDomains = dynamic([
    "gmail.com","outlook.com","yahoo.com","icloud.com","hotmail.com","qq.com",
    "protonmail.com","aol.com","zoho.com","mail.com","gmx.com","yandex.com",
    "tutanota.com","mail.ru","live.com","msn.com","naver.com","163.com",
    "ymail.com","fastmail.com","sky.com","bt.com"
]);
EmailAttachmentInfo
// Attachment name contains risky terms
| where FileName has_any (SensitiveWords)
// Extract recipient domain (case-insensitive safe)
| extend RecipientDomain = tolower(extract(@"@(.+)$", 1, RecipientEmailAddress))
// Exclude internal recipients and specific allow pattern
| where RecipientDomain !in~ (InternalDomains)
      and RecipientEmailAddress !contains 'talkinthebay'

| where RecipientDomain in~ (PersonalDomains)

    FileSizeMB = round(FileSize / 1048576.0, 2),
    RiskLevel = case(
        FileSize > 50000000, "HIGH",     // >50MB
        FileSize > 10000000, "MEDIUM",   // >10MB

    // Extract the matched sensitive word for context
    MatchedKeyword = extract_all(@"(Customer|Kundenliste|Klient|Kund|Klant|Client|Kunde|Cliente|kokayku|Kuraianto|Risuto|Clienti|prospect|prospetti|Interessentenliste|prospekt|enrich|Angereichert|Enriquecido|Arricchito|Berik|Beriget|Rikastettu|portfolio|Portefeuille|Portfölj)", FileName)[0]

    TimeGenerated,

    RiskLevel,

properties.displayName: [Exfiltration] Leavers Uploading File To Cloud
properties.description:
This alert looks for users in the High_Risk_Watchlist who upload files to cloud destinations
(as recorded in CloudAppEvents). Investigate the activity, the destination domain, and the label,
and determine whether data exfiltration risk exists.
properties.query:
// Case-insensitive watchlist match (High Risk users / leavers)
let HighRisk = _GetWatchlist('High_Risk_Watchlist') | project SearchKey = tolower(tostring(SearchKey));

CloudAppEvents
// Normalize principal for case-insensitive comparison
| extend AccountDisplayNameLower = tolower(AccountDisplayName)
| where AccountDisplayNameLower in (HighRisk)

// Normalize and extract fields from RawEventData
| extend
    operation          = tostring(RawEventData.Operation),
    UploadDomainRaw    = tostring(RawEventData.TargetDomain),
    UploadURL          = tostring(RawEventData.TargetUrl),
    ObjectID1          = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectId),
    DeviceID           = tostring(RawEventData.DeviceName),
    FileExtension      = tostring(RawEventData.FileExtension),
    Application1       = tostring(RawEventData.Application),
    EnforcementModeRaw = tostring(RawEventData.EnforcementMode),
    SensitivityLabel   = tostring(RawEventData.SensitivityLabelEventData),
    PolicyInfo         = tostring(RawEventData.PolicyMatchInfo),
    DLPDetails         = todynamic(RawEventData.DlpAuditEventMetadata)

// Only file uploads to cloud operation
| where operation contains 'FileUploadedToCloud'

// Derived fields
| extend
    EvaluationTime = tostring(DLPDetails.EvaluationTime),
    // Human-readable sensitivity label names
    LabelName = case(
      SensitivityLabel == "6b471bfd-f628-4d09-bd36-e4014ade38e5", "Limited Access - Internal Staff Only",
      SensitivityLabel == "2bc8e810-0e48-4510-a73b-a00cf068b73d", "Creditsafe Eyes Only",
      SensitivityLabel == "08181d91-44f1-4c8a-a789-226d3eeb0820", "Limited Access - External and Internal",
      SensitivityLabel == "900e61c5-9326-4775-9dd5-9a546e043cca", "Public (Anyone Can View)",
      tostring(SensitivityLabel)
    ),
    // Map enforcement mode (1=Allowed, 4=Blocked), fallback to raw value
    Action = case(
      EnforcementModeRaw == "1", "Allowed",
      EnforcementModeRaw == "4", "Blocked",
      tostring(EnforcementModeRaw)
    ),
    UploadDomain = tolower(UploadDomainRaw)

// Exclusions (normalize to lowercase for in~ / contains)
// NOTE: Some entries are not full FQDNs (e.g., "blackline"); these behave as substring-type excludes in practice.
| where UploadDomain !in~ (
    "eu-west-1.console.aws.amazon.com",
    "csceproduction.crm4.dynamics.com",
    "prod1.ar-eu.blackline.com",
    "apps.docusign.com",
    "central.connect.pwc.com",
    "dev.azure.com",
    "acrobat.adobe.com",
    "chatgpt.com"
  )
// Exclude broader strings that may appear inside domains
| where UploadDomain !contains 'blackline'
| where UploadDomain !contains 'recruiterflow'
| where UploadDomain !contains 'pwc'
// Exclude any creditsafe-owned destinations
| where UploadDomain !contains 'creditsafe'

| project
    CreationTime       = TimeGenerated,
    UploadDomain,
    UploadURL,
    PolicyInfo,
    LabelName,
    Action,
    FileName           = ObjectID1,
    FileExtension,
    Application1,
    City,
    CountryCode,
    IPAddress,
    AccountDisplayName,
    DeviceID,
    ActionType

The file name always contains the Base64 string "IyNURVhUTlVNUkFORE9NNDUjIw,".

properties.displayName: MFA Fatigue
properties.description: This alert identifies potential multi-factor authentication (MFA) fatigue attacks, a tactic where threat actors repeatedly send MFA push notifications to a user in hopes of tricking them into approving one. This technique is commonly used in credential-stuffing or phishing campaigns after initial access is gained.
properties.query:
let WhiteListed_Accounts = dynamic([""]);
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationRequirement == "multiFactorAuthentication"
| where UserPrincipalName !in (WhiteListed_Accounts)
| summarize PromptCount = count() by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where PromptCount > 20

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: MFA Alert Fatigue for one or more Users
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat:
This alert detects potential multi-factor authentication (MFA) fatigue attacks, where more than 20 MFA prompts are triggered within a 1-minute window. This behavior may indicate an attempt by a threat actor to overwhelm a user with repeated MFA requests in hopes of eliciting an accidental or fatigued approval.

Recommended Investigation Steps:

Review the sign-in logs for the affected user(s) to determine whether any MFA prompts were approved.

Confirm with the user whether the approvals were intentional.

Assess whether the account shows signs of compromise, such as unusual login locations, IP addresses, or device fingerprints.

properties.description:
This rule will check if a sign-in failed into LastPass due to MFA.
An incident can indicate the potential brute forcing of a LastPass account. 
The use of MFA is identified by combining the sign-in logs, this rule assumes LastPass is federated to AAD.

| where ResultType in (50074, 50076)

ABNORMAL_THREAT_MESSAGES_CL

properties.displayName: Detect Potential Kerberoast Activities
properties.description:
This query aim to detect if someone requests service tickets (where count => maxcount)
The query requires trimming to set a baseline level for MaxCount  
Mitre Technique: Kerberoasting (T1558.003)
@MattiasBorg82
properties.query:
let MaxCount = 70; //Number of requests per 2 minute timeframe, depending on org size.
IdentityLogonEvents
| where ActionType == "LogonSuccess"
| where Protocol == "Kerberos"
| extend json = todynamic(parse_json(tostring(AdditionalFields)))
| extend SPN = json.Spns,
       AttackTechniques = json.AttackTechniques
      | project-away json
| where isnotempty(SPN)
| where AttackTechniques has "T1558.003"
| mv-expand SPN
        | extend SPNType = tostring(extract(@"^\w+",0,tostring(SPN)))
| distinct tostring(SPN), DeviceName, AccountUpn, AccountSid, bin(TimeGenerated, 2m), ReportId, tostring(AttackTechniques)
| summarize count(), SPNS=(make_list(SPN, 100000)),ReportId=tostring((make_list(ReportId, 100000))[0]) by AccountUpn,AccountSid,DeviceName, bin(TimeGenerated, 2m), tostring(AttackTechniques)
| extend SPNS = (replace_regex(tostring(SPNS), @'[^\w+-\/]+', '')) 
| where count_ >= MaxCount
| extend HostName = iff(DeviceName has '.', substring(DeviceName, 0, indexof(DeviceName, '.')), DeviceName)
| extend DnsDomain = iff(DeviceName has '.', substring(DeviceName, indexof(DeviceName, '.') + 1), "")
| extend AccountDomain = tostring(split(AccountUpn, '@')[1]), AccountName = tostring(split(AccountUpn, '@')[0])

properties.displayName: Potential Kerberoasting Attack
properties.description:
This alert indicates a potential Kerberoasting attack detected within the network. Kerberoasting is a technique used by attackers to extract service account credentials from the Kerberos authentication protocol. The attacker requests service tickets for service accounts, which are then cracked offline to reveal plaintext passwords. This type of attack can lead to unauthorized access to sensitive systems and data.

Kerberoasting is a type of cyber attack that targets the Kerberos authentication protocol used in many enterprise environments. The goal of this attack is to obtain the hashed credentials of service accounts, which can then be cracked offline to reveal the plaintext passwords.
properties.query:
let WhitelistAdminAccount = dynamic(["svc_appviewx@creditsafe.com", "safeservice@creditsafeuk.com"]);
IdentityLogonEvents 
| where Protocol == "Kerberos"
| where parse_json(AdditionalFields)["AttackTechniques"] has 'T1558.003'
| where parse_json(AdditionalFields)["EncryptionType"] has "rc4hmac"
| extend SPNs = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields)["Spns"])
| where not (AccountUpn has_any(WhitelistAdminAccount))
| where AccountName !contains "svc_solarwinds_orion"
